pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis (Paraneoplastic, secondary to ovarian teratoma) THE SMOKING GUN: The clinical triad of acute psychosis progressing to facial dyskinesias with central hypoventilation, accompanied by the EEG extreme delta brush pattern and an underlying ovarian teratoma. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: The patient's ectopic neural tissue inside the ovarian teratoma expresses GluN1 subunits of the N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor. The host immune system mounts an IgG autoimmune response against these target antigens. These circulating autoantibodies cross the blood-brain barrier and bind to neuronal NMDA receptors in the brain, causing receptor cross-linking and internalisation (downregulation). This loss of functional NMDA receptors disinhibits cortical networks (specifically via suppression of GABAergic interneurons), triggering psychiatric manifestations, movement disorders, autonomic instability, and central respiratory failure. Treatment requires tumor resection alongside aggressive immunotherapy (plasma exchange, IVIG, and rituximab).
